correctness.rationale: Taking the source scalar calculus as the load-bearing theorem, the remainder is exact. The labels by positive dyadic rationals are exhaustive and unique; direct sum sends \((q,r)\) to \(q+r\), so the internal degree structure is the positive additive dyadic semigroup. Its Grothendieck group is \(\mathbb Z[1/2]\). Any additive automorphism is fixed by \(c=F(1)\), and dyadic divisibility gives \(F(q)=cq\); surjectivity forces \(c\) to be a positive unit of \(\mathbb Z[1/2]\), hence \(c=2^z\). The stabilizer of \(1\) is therefore trivial.
